answer: The Commission disputes the false allegations contained in the report published on 3 February 2026 by the Committee on the Judiciary of the US House of Representatives. The Code of Conduct on Disinformation (1) is a voluntary tool set up by its signatories. The meetings organised by the Code’s permanent Taskforce are meetings of the signatories.

All relevant information concerning the Code, as well as a list of its signatories, is available in the Transparency Centre (2). The Digital Services Act (DSA (3)) does not define what constitutes illegal content; this is the exclusive reserve of national or EU legislation. The Commission does not have the power to order platforms to remove specific content.

Decisions concerning the retention or removal of content are made by the providers themselves, in accordance with their own terms and conditions of use, including for the video content to which you refer. However, the DSA requires online platform services to provide a clear and specific explanation of the reasons for restricting or removing content and to offer effective remedies to users.
If a user believes they have been wronged, the DSA thus allows them to easily access redress mechanisms that are unparalleled in the world. 1
